accepted.s:
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was awarded the title ‘Vidyasagar’ primarily for his
1. Sanskrit learning
2. Leadership of the Arya Samaj
3. Contributions to modern Bengali prose
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: The title ‘Vidyasagar’, meaning ‘Ocean of Learning’, was associated with his exceptional Sanskrit learning. He also modernised Bengali prose, but the Arya Samaj was not his organisation.
accepted.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing the person’s documented achievements from an unrelated organisation.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: Which of the following positions was held by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar?
o: Head Pandit at Fort William College
accepted.x: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar served as Head Pandit at Fort William College. Kesari was associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak, while the other positions are not attributed to Vidyasagar here.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who held this position?’ method and reject offices associated with other reformers.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a distinctive step taken by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar as Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta?
o: He shifted it from Calcutta to Bombay.
He restricted admission to Brahmin students.
He converted it into a girls’ school exclusively.
He opened the institution to non-Brahmin students.
accepted.x: As Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Vidyasagar opened the institution to non-Brahmin students.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional reform directly, using reversed admission policy as the main trap.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:
1. He campaigned against child marriage.
2. He opposed polygamy.
3. His social reform activities were confined to widow remarriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Vidyasagar campaigned against both child marriage and polygamy. His activities were not confined to widow remarriage.
accepted.tq: Find the single over-restrictive statement containing ‘confined’.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: Who sent a message of support for Veeresalingam’s third widow remarriage?
accepted.x: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar sent a message of support for Veeresalingam’s third widow remarriage.
accepted.tq: Match the reformer with the specific act of support rather than with a general reform campaign.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Indian Spectator — Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s Sanskrit grammar
Notes on Infant Marriage — Vidyasagar’s autobiography
accepted.x: Barnaparichay was a Bengali alphabet primer written by Vidyasagar. The other works or journals are wrongly attributed or misdescribed.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and reject swapped authorship or genre.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: The Bethune School was established with the support of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and:
accepted.x: Vidyasagar helped J.E.D. Bethune establish the Bethune School in 1849, one of the earliest girls’ schools in India.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–institution association and distinguish it from later women’s education figures.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s: In which year was the Bethune School, associated with Vidyasagar’s work for women’s education, established?
accepted.x: The Bethune School was established in 1849 with the support of J.E.D. Bethune and Vidyasagar.
accepted.tq: Separate the school’s establishment year from the later years of widow-remarriage and women’s organisations.
accepted.sec: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar - campaigns, books, Bethune School, title

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Organisation)
a. Arya Mahila Samaj
b. Ladies’ Social Conference
c. Bharat Stree Mahamandal
 d. Women’s Indian Association
List-II (Year)
i. 1882
ii. 1904
iii. 1910
iv. 1917
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Arya Mahila Samaj was established in 1882, Ladies’ Social Conference in 1904, Bharat Stree Mahamandal in 1910 and the Women’s Indian Association in 1917.
accepted.tq: Start from the earliest sure pair and match the remaining organisations by chronology.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also known as Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with:
accepted.x: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also called Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with Ramabai Ranade in Bombay in 1904 and functioned under the National Social Conference.
accepted.tq: Use the full organisation name, founder and location to avoid confusing similarly themed bodies.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Bharat Stree Mahamandal is correct?
o: It was founded in 1927 by Margaret Cousins at Bombay.
It was founded in 1904 by Ramabai Ranade at Poona.
It was founded in 1917 by Annie Besant at Madras.
It was founded in 1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani at Allahabad.
accepted.x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal was founded in 1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani at Allahabad. It is regarded as the first major all-India women’s body founded by a woman.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–place–year triad and reject swapped details from other organisations.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Bharat Stree Mahamandal is significant because it was:
o: The first organisation to press for the Sarda Act
The first major all-India women’s body founded by a woman
The first women’s organisation formed exclusively for Muslim education
The first women’s university in India
accepted.x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal, founded by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani, is regarded as the first major all-India women’s body founded by a woman.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise distinguishing description instead of accepting a broad women’s-education label.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Anjuman-e-Khawatin-e-Islam, established in 1914, was primarily associated with:
o: The campaign against polygamy in Madras
accepted.x: Anjuman-e-Khawatin-e-Islam, established in 1914, was associated with Muslim women’s education.
accepted.tq: Link the organisation’s distinctive community focus with its correct year.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the establishment of the Women’s Indian Association in Madras in 1917?
o: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani and Ramabai Ranade
accepted.x: The Women’s Indian Association was established in Madras in 1917 by Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins.
accepted.tq: Use the paired-founder pattern and distinguish it from the founders of later organisations.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Women’s Indian Association — 1917 — Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins
National Council of Women in India — 1925 — Meherbai Tata and Cornelia Sorabji
All India Women’s Conference — 1927 — Margaret Cousins
Bharat Stree Mahamandal — 1925 — Sarala Devi Chaudhurani
accepted.x: Bharat Stree Mahamandal was established in 1910, not 1925. The National Council of Women in India, the AIWC and the WIA are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped year in the not-correctly-matched option.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s:
Arrange the following women’s organisations in chronological order of establishment:
A. Women’s Indian Association
B. Arya Mahila Samaj
C. All India Women’s Conference
D. Bharat Stree Mahamandal
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Arya Mahila Samaj (1882), Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910), Women’s Indian Association (1917), and All India Women’s Conference (1927).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest organisations first, then place the two intermediate bodies.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s:
The All India Women’s Conference, established in 1927, pressed for which of the following measures?
1. Sarda Act, 1929
2. Hindu Women’s Right to Property Act, 1937
3. Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act, 1856
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The AIWC pressed for the Sarda Act of 1929 and the Hindu Women’s Right to Property Act of 1937. The Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act had been enacted in 1856 and is not listed as one of these AIWC measures.
accepted.tq: Use the dates to eliminate the older law and retain the two later legislative campaigns.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the attribution of Bharat Stree Mahamandal is correct?
o: The standard attribution is exclusively to D.K. Karve, with no association with Sarala Devi Chaudhurani.
The standard attribution is to Sarala Devi Chaudhurani, although D.K. Karve is credited on one account.
It was founded by Meherbai Tata and Cornelia Sorabji in Bombay.
It was founded jointly by Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins in Madras.
accepted.x: The standard attribution is to Sarala Devi Chaudhurani, who founded Bharat Stree Mahamandal at Allahabad in 1910. One account credits D.K. Karve, but that is not the standard attribution.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the standard attribution and a conflicting secondary attribution.
accepted.sec: Women's organisations → year

accepted.s: Behramji Malabari’s work Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood was published in:
accepted.x: Behramji Malabari published Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood in 1884 while campaigning against child marriage and enforced widowhood.
accepted.tq: Separate the reformer’s publication year from the later Phulmoni case and Age of Consent Act.

accepted.s: Which journal was edited by Behramji Malabari?
accepted.x: Behramji Malabari edited the Indian Spectator. Kesari was associated with Tilak, while the other titles are not the journal identified here as his.
accepted.tq: Apply the editor–journal association and avoid substituting a journal linked with another reformer.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the Rakhmabai case?
o: A husband’s suit for restitution of conjugal rights after a child marriage
A case concerning the abolition of sati
A dispute over admission to the Bethune School
A petition against the licensing of women doctors
accepted.x: Rakhmabai’s husband, Dadaji, sued for restitution of conjugal rights after their child marriage. The case raised questions concerning age of consent and conjugal rights.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal issue rather than choosing a broader but unrelated social-reform theme.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Rakhmabai later became one of India’s first practising women doctors. The Rakhmabai case occurred during:
accepted.x: The Rakhmabai case took place from 1884 to 1888. Rakhmabai subsequently became one of India’s first practising women doctors.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date range of the Rakhmabai litigation from that of the Phulmoni Dasi case.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: The Phulmoni Dasi case is generally placed in which period?
accepted.x: The Phulmoni Dasi case occurred in 1889–1890 and preceded the Age of Consent Act of 1891.
accepted.tq: Use the sequence of case, debate and legislation to distinguish the date range.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Age of Consent Act, 1891:
1. It raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to 12.
2. It regulated consummation rather than directly fixing the minimum age of marriage.
3. It was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1891 Act raised the age of consent from 10 to 12, dealt with consummation rather than directly regulating marriage, and was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the distinction between consent and marriage.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Age of Consent Act, 1891 from a marriage law?
o: It abolished child marriage throughout India.
It fixed the minimum marriage age for both boys and girls at 18.
It regulated consummation and did not directly fix the minimum age of marriage.
It dealt exclusively with widow remarriage.
accepted.x: The 1891 Act regulated the age of consent for consummation; it did not directly establish a minimum age of marriage.
accepted.tq: Test the precise legal meaning of consent instead of accepting a broad marriage-law description.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Who among the following opposed the Age of Consent Bill on the ground that it represented foreign interference in Hindu custom?
accepted.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed the Bill, including through Kesari, on the ground that it was foreign interference in Hindu custom. The Moderates supported the Bill.
accepted.tq: Use the reformer–position contrast, particularly the opposition of Tilak versus the support of the Moderates.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments concerning the age of consent in chronological order:
A. Age of consent raised to 16 through an amendment to the Indian Penal Code
B. Age of consent raised to 18
C. Age of Consent Act raised the age from 10 to 12
D. Age of consent raised to 14
accepted.x: The sequence is 1891: 10 to 12; 1925: 14; 1949: 16; and 2012: 18 under POCSO.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the 1891 Act and the latest 2012 milestone, then place the intermediate amendments.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a later change in the age of consent?
o: 1925 — age raised to 14 through an Indian Penal Code amendment
2012 — age raised to 16 under the Indian Penal Code
2023 — age reduced to 16 under Section 63 of the BNS
accepted.x: In 1925, an Indian Penal Code amendment raised the age of consent to 14. It was raised to 16 in 1949 and to 18 under POCSO in 2012; BNS 2023 Section 63 retains 18.
accepted.tq: Reject reversed trends and wrong statutory associations by checking the direction of each age change.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak

accepted.s: Under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the age of consent is retained at:
accepted.x: BNS 2023 Section 63 retains the age of consent at 18 years, consistent with the position under POCSO 2012.
accepted.tq: Use the latest statutory figure and distinguish it from earlier historical ages.
accepted.sec: Age-of-consent debates - Rakhmabai, Phulmoni, Malabari, Tilak
